test_condition: Course uses low-consequence practice, no attempt telemetry, learner-paced navigation and offline resumption.
expected_resolution: Runtime profile resolves without AI or research instrumentation; only functional state persists.

scenario: Personal reflective study with optional analytics
test_condition: Learner enables goals/reflection and personal analytics but does not share them.
expected_resolution: Opt-in values apply at learner scope; visibility remains personal; no institutional/research access is inferred.

test_condition: Author sets sequence and feedback while learners control pace within allowed choices.
expected_resolution: Course policy governs structure; learner choices apply within permitted space; accessibility overrides remain available.

scenario: Formal mastery course with soft prerequisites
test_condition: Progression uses criterion evidence, remediation, override and recheck.
expected_resolution: Structural completion is not mastery; criterion version and evidence scope are snapshotted; no universal threshold is assumed.

test_condition: Institution requires limited attempts, scoring and prerequisite gates.
expected_resolution: Consequential policy is explicit; accessibility and due-process rules outrank institutional defaults; AI cannot be sole authority.

test_condition: Two derived courses vary information concentration while claiming equivalent scope.
expected_resolution: Protocol locks content/configuration/composition/instruments; explicit diffs and provenance identify intended and accidental differences.

test_condition: Participants receive conditions in different orders.
expected_resolution: Assignment, sequence snapshot, instruments and analysis plan are versioned; carryover and order remain methodological concerns.

scenario: Accessibility accommodation conflicts with research condition
test_condition: Participant requires a modality or time accommodation not predeclared in the condition.
expected_resolution: Rights/accessibility override applies; construct/comparability impact is documented; participation cannot depend on unnecessary disclosure.

scenario: GPT+MCP construction with ARA situated repair
test_condition: GPT builds a part, user comments on one card in ARA, GPT repairs only that target and a re-audit follows.
expected_resolution: Entry channel and target are preserved; semantic repair creates a revision; audit and repair remain separate; publication requires human action.

scenario: Reused microsequence receives an upstream update
test_condition: A referenced unit changes while several published courses use older revisions.
expected_resolution: Consumers are notified and shown impact/diff; no silent propagation; each course may accept, fork or retain its snapshot.

test_condition: Course combines original, adapted and third-party assets.
expected_resolution: Licenses and attribution are recorded per scope; compatibility ambiguity blocks publication pending qualified review.

test_condition: GPT needs context from another restricted workspace.
expected_resolution: Confidentiality and role authorization outrank convenience; chat memory grants no access; context snapshot excludes unauthorized material.

scenario: Unavailable connected capability during offline use
test_condition: AI or connected validator is unavailable after materialization.
expected_resolution: Capability is explicitly unavailable or an approved deterministic fallback is used; no silent lower-quality substitution changes the condition.

test_condition: A participant withdraws while a course version and pseudonymized research record exist.
expected_resolution: Withdrawal policy, content lifecycle and research retention are resolved separately; access is revoked as required and retained records follow approved purpose/retention rules.

scenario: Institutional publication with separation of duties
test_condition: Author requests publication after AI audit but without accessibility and licensing review.
expected_resolution: Publication gate remains blocked; AI audit cannot substitute qualified reviews; required approvals must reference the reviewed revision.
